messages:
ben_sales: Heads-up — prospect redlined the agreement and added an MFN + 12-month price protection clause, plus a per-token cap for hosted usage. Need deal-desk + legal input. Excerpt below:

```text
5.2 Most-Favored-Nation: Customer shall be entitled to the most favorable pricing terms offered by Provider to any third party for substantially similar services.
6.1 Price Protection: Provider will not increase Customer prices for 12 months from Effective Date.
```

ben_sales: They also asked for a cap on per-token price at $0.015 for any public promotions. POC starts next week, so timing is tight. @carla_legal @dina_dealdesk @eric_ps

dina_dealdesk: Yikes. MFN + price protection is risky for us.
- MFN could force us to match any future sitewide promos or PLG credits.
- Price protection for 12 months removes our ability to manage rate card changes.
Options I recommend: 1) Narrow MFN to "materially comparable customers" and same region/plan. 2) Exclude time-limited promos under $50k. 3) Swap 12-month price protection for a defined commit with a discount schedule.

dina_dealdesk: If they want a true 12-month hold we should require a minimum committed spend (e.g., $100k ARR) and tier the discount. Otherwise we'd be locking pricing for low revenue.

carla_legal: I can draft counterlanguage — propose a limited MFN: applies only to commercial terms for substantially similar volume commitments and excludes one-off promotional discounts. Also add a carve-out: internal sales promotions, trial credits, and open beta offers excluded.

eric_ps: Technical / POC note: their POC runs at higher qps and will inflate token consumption. If MFN applies across all usage levels, we might be exposed when we later optimize pricing or offer new bundles. We need a true-up clause and also to tie MFN to committed units or revenue buckets.

maya_sales_engineering: Quick back-of-envelope: our list hosted gen price = $0.02/token. If we give a 20% committed discount, that’s $0.016/token. With MFN they'd expect that for comparable customers. If they demand a $0.015 cap for promos, margin drops. Example: 6.25M tokens/month at $0.016 ≈ $100k/mo gross.

ben_sales: Good points. Prospect is pushing for enterprise terms but wants hosted simplicity. They won't sign a Dedicated commitment. Can we offer a "hosted commit" structure?

dina_dealdesk: Yes — propose a 12-month hosted commit (prepaid credits) in exchange for a limited price hold. Terms: 1) Commit size determines discount bands, 2) MFN limited to same API package & region, 3) No retroactive refunds for short tactical promos (<$50k) and no obligation for beta programs. I'll draft pricing bands for approval.

carla_legal: I'll prepare redline: narrow MFN + carve-outs + explicit no-retro clause for promos. I'll push language that MFN only applies to the published rate card for sustained commercial offers (>= 90 days). That prevents them from claiming temporary marketing discounts.

eric_ps: Also request a restriction: MFN doesn't apply to feature-differentiated offers (e.g., Dedicated vs Hosted), and doesn't compel us to open private beta pricing to them.

ben_sales: Thanks. Could you both that — @dina_dealdesk can you escalate to revenue ops for the commit threshold approval? If commit < $100k we'd treat price hold as max 90 days.

dina_dealdesk: Will do — I'll loop in revops. Tentative ask: approve 3-tier commit bands (50k, 100k, 250k) with corresponding discounts; fallback: 90d price hold for <100k.

carla_legal: I'll send a draft counter by EOD with the suggested carve-outs.

ben_sales: Perfect. I'll respond to the customer with "under review" and push POC start if we get verbal go. :thumbsup:

maya_sales_engineering: If you want a quick template for hosted commits I can drop one in the thread.

ben_sales: Please do.

dina_dealdesk: Escalated to revops (cc). Will update when they sign off on commit bands. :eyes:

carla_legal: Marking this high priority.

ben_sales: Thanks all — will wait for redline and commit bands before final reply.
